the optical properties of nanocrystals can be engineered by the choice of material composition, shape and surface passivation, which can result in efficient single-photon sources at room temperature.
we have developed a new approach for engineering of radiative and multi-exciton channels in colloidal quantum dots.
the optical properties of colloidal nanocrystal can be engineered to produce room-temperature efficient sources of single photon, with high brightness and low blinking probability.

the design of colloidal quantum dots with tailored optical properties.
the engineering of the optical properties of colloidal quantum dots, in order to achieve efficient single photon sources at room temperature.
the design and synthesis of colloidal nanocrystal quantum dots (QDs).

the dot-in-rods nanocrystals are a very interesting system, which allows the tuning of the emission properties, the blinking and the multi-excitonic emissions.
we have demonstrated a new class of quantum dots with unprecedented properties, which are of interest for quantum technologies.

we have developed a new class of quantum sources, based on colloidal nanorods, that are able to overcome the main limitation of quantum dots, i.e. the blinking, and to provide a high efficiency of single photon emission at room temperature.

we are able to tune the radiative and nonradiative processes in colloidal nanomaterials by tuning their size and shape, and we have demonstrated the possibility to obtain single photon sources on demand.
the engineering of the radiative and nonradiative channels in colloids is a key factor for the development of new generation of nanoscale light emitters.

the engineering of nanocrystals can be used as a tool for controlling the radiative and nonradiative channels, and thus to tune both the emission efficiency and blinking effect.
the shell thickness is a crucial parameter for engineering the radiative and nonradiative channels of colloidal nanocrystal emitters.
the control of the shell dimension allows to tune the emission wavelength, the quantum yield and the blinking behavior of the nanocrystals.
